page: OVHcloud r2-120 is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an Intel Haswell x86_64 processor. The configuration allocates 8 dedicated physical cores clocked at 2.2 GHz with one thread per core, supported by 16 MB of Level 3 cache. Memory allocation is high at 120 GB of RAM, equating to 15 GB per dedicated core. Local storage is bundled as a 200 GB SSD, paired with a 1 Gbps baseline network connection. Acceleration hardware is omitted, with zero GPUs present on the instance.

Benchmark evaluations highlight the older Intel Haswell architectural baseline. Single-thread execution is modest, reflected by a stress-ng score of 804.33 and a Geekbench single-core score of 980. Multi-core performance reaches middle-tier levels, scoring 4700 on Geekbench and 8598.23 on the PassMark CPU test. Memory subsystem benchmarks show high cached throughput at 582.18 GB/s for small blocks, though uncached large-block write bandwidth drops to 12.56 GB/s. For in-memory key-value processing, the server demonstrates solid throughput, sustaining 8.58 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r2-120 leverages mature enterprise hardware to deliver substantial RAM density without the premium cost associated with bleeding-edge compute architectures. The trade-off is diminished floating-point and instruction-per-cycle throughput, rendering the server less suitable for compute-heavy workloads or LLM generation. Instead, the platform is structured for memory-demanding applications requiring significant working sets with predictable compute needs, including distributed in-memory caching systems, intermediate database stores, and RAM-heavy staging environments.
description: OVHcloud r2-120 is a memory-optimized cloud instance powered by an 8-core Intel Haswell processor clocked at 2.2 GHz, featuring 8 dedicated single-threaded physical cores on an x86_64 architecture. The server is equipped with 120 GB of RAM, yielding an expansive 15 GB per core allocation. Local storage includes a bundled 200 GB SSD, alongside 1 Gbps baseline networking and zero GPUs. In benchmark assessments, the older Haswell CPU produces modest single-core throughput, such as a 980 Geekbench single-core score, but sustains average multi-core capability with an 8598.23 PassMark CPU score and 8.58 million Redis SET operations per second. Uncached memory writes are constrained at 12.56 GB/s. By utilizing mature hardware, the r2-120 delivers high RAM capacity at a moderate cost tier, serving as a practical deployment for memory-bound applications, large Redis caching clusters, intermediate relational databases, and RAM-heavy data preprocessing pipelines.
